questions.q: In the lab scenario, what mechanism fixes agents closing tickets with nothing recorded about what fixed them?
options: Adding a brand-new field called Fix Notes
Deleting the Resolved state entirely
Setting Priority to Critical on every incident
A Data Policy conditioned on state = Resolved, making Resolution Code and Close Notes mandatory, plus blocking the New-to-Closed jump
questions.explain: Resolution Code and Close Notes already exist on incident — the fix is enforcing them at the right point, and blocking the state-skip.

questions.q: Before populating the Priority Lookup Rule matrix for the 500-person company, what must be confirmed first?
options: That the business's own definitions of Impact 1/2/3 and Urgency 1/2/3 actually match what the matrix will assume
That the default matrix should always be used as-is
That manual override is permanently disabled
That Assignment Groups have been deleted
questions.explain: Populating the matrix without confirming what Impact/Urgency actually mean to this business risks a matrix nobody trusts.

questions.q: How does the lab scenario verify the state model is actually enforced, not just configured?
options: By reading the Data Policy record and assuming it works
By testing: try moving a test incident New-to-Closed directly, and try moving it to Resolved with Resolution Code blank, confirming both are refused
By asking the service desk lead to confirm verbally
By checking that the incident table extends task
questions.explain: Actually attempting the bad transitions and confirming the platform refuses them is the real verification step.

questions.q: Why does the lab configure round robin for Network Operations instead of a fixed Assigned To?
options: Round robin is required by the platform and cannot be turned off
To rotate new Network incidents across the group's six agents instead of overloading whoever's name sorts first
Round robin removes the need for an Assignment Group entirely
Fixed assignment is actually faster to configure and was used instead
questions.explain: Round robin spreads newly routed incidents across the group instead of piling onto one agent.

questions.q: Why does the lab's Major Incident threshold combine Priority 1 with 'affecting more than 50 users' instead of using Priority alone?
options: Because user count is the only field that matters for Priority
Because Priority cannot be Critical for any incident affecting fewer than 50 users
Because major_incident_state only exists for incidents with low Priority
Because a single Priority 1 affecting one person (e.g. one executive's laptop) shouldn't trigger a war room and full MIM process
questions.explain: A multi-factor threshold avoids declaring Major Incident status for cases that don't actually need war-room-level coordination.
